1. Introduction
"The Hobbit" is a famous fantasy novel written by J.R.R.
It was adapted into a film trilogy, directed by Peter Jackson and released between 2012 and 2014.
There have been various arguments about which version - the book or the movie - is better.
This essay will attempt to examine the book and the movie versions and compare them with regard to the story events, political and social imagery, and general changes that were made.
2. Events Deleted or Changed in the Movie
a Smaug s Attack
In the book, there is the event of Smaug’s attack on the dwarves, where it is stated that he would burn all the doors with his fire and destroy everything inside the mountain.
However, this scene was completely removed from the movie.
In addition, in the book Smaug also had a conversation with Bilbo, while this scene did not exist in the movie.
b) Bilbo’s Escape in a Mole Hole
Bilbo had the chance to escape the spiders’ web, when they were not looking at him, and he did so by hiding in a mole hole, in the book.
However, in the movie, Bilbo could not escape from the web without help, because the spiders did not let him do it.
c) Bane of Babes of Babador
Bilbo, Thorin and company went through a long tunnel under a river, and the name of their companion that died along the way was Bane of Babes of Babador, while in the movie this was changed to Bifur.
**Critical Review on *The Light in their Eyes* by Sonia Nieto and *Reflective Teaching: An Introduction* by Kenneth Zeichner and Daniel Liston: Critical Essay**

This paper will critically review the books "The Light in Their Eyes: Hispanic Students in an Urban School" by Sonia Nieto (1974) and "Reflective Teaching: An Introduction" by Kenneth Zeichner and Daniel Liston (2018).
The critical review will focus on the content of each book, their strengths, their weaknesses and how they can be applied in teaching.
### Part 1: Review of "The Light in Their Eyes"
#### 1.1 Background
Sonia Nieto wrote "The Light in Their Eyes" which was published in 1974, when she was still a graduate student, and her advisor, Juan Pedro Lozano, asked her to write a dissertation.
She spent some time studying students in two schools for Mexican Americans (Nieto, 1974).
#### 1.2 Content of Book

In this book, Nieto gives a description of two schools, one school called "Ricardo Montalbán High School" that serves mainly poor Mexicans and is in East Los Angeles, and the other is "H. Rap Brown Middle School" that serves Blacks, poor Latinos, and low income Asians.
The main idea here is to show that both schools have students that suffer from poverty and that they are also in a minority, even if there are some white students attending one of the schools.
### Importance of Conserving Electricity: An Academic Essay
#### Abstract
Conserving electricity is extremely important as it reduces the consumption of non-renewable resources.

This research paper will discuss the importance of conserving electricity in terms of saving money, saving resources, improving the environment, improving the electric grid, protecting the planet, and protecting the climate.
The essay will end with some suggestions on how to save energy.
#### Introduction
In this 21st century, it is impossible to imagine the modern world without electricity.
Electricity makes people's everyday lives easier and more convenient, and it is necessary for work, study, cooking, cleaning, medical care, production, transportation, etc.
However, as we use more and more electricity, there are more and more problems with the electric power system, like blackouts.
We should conserve electricity in our daily lives and at work so that we can reduce the consumption of non-renewable and limited energy and protect the environment.
In this essay, I will talk about why we should conserve electricity.
#### Saving Money
The first reason for saving electricity is to save money.
If you save electricity at home, you can get a bill from your power company that has a lower amount than usual, and when the company bills you a lower amount for your power, you have saved money.
For example, if your house normally uses ten hundred kilowatt-hours (kWh) of power, but you save 20% of that (200 kWh), you would pay less money for 800 kWh instead of 1000 kWh.
#### Save Resources
Another reason to save electricity is to save resources.
There are a lot of ways that we can use to produce power.
Some of them are clean, but some are not.
For example, when we use coal or oil to make power, a lot of carbon dioxide comes out, which makes the air dirty and bad for our health.
**The Social Impact of Zip Codes on Human Health**
In the modern world, social differences between groups of people exist on various bases and often cause inequalities.

While some of those inequalities are related to characteristics such as race, gender, or age, this essay will be looking at how a factor which may not immediately seem like it should impact someone’s health (their zip code) impacts human health.
In recent years, there has been research that has looked into how the physical area in which you live can impact your health.
It has been found that people living in certain zip codes in the USA have much higher rates of being ill than people who live in other zip codes.
This research shows that the zip code that a person lives in does impact their health.
The purpose of this essay is to investigate this idea.

The first part of this essay will be discussing the different reasons why a person lives in a certain zip code, these reasons will be followed up with examples of which groups of people tend to live in certain zip codes.
The second part of the essay will be talking about how the zip codes impact the health of the people living in them and the evidence for this theory.
Following this, the essay will discuss what should be done about it, and finish with a conclusion.

### Antiferroelectricity and Antiferroelectric Materials Report
#### Table of Contents
1. Abstract

4. Lead Zirconate

Abstract
This report provides an overview of antiferroelectricity and antiferroelectric materials.
It starts with a short introduction to the topic and discusses the properties of antiferroelectric materials in terms of their polarization and domain structures.

This is followed by a discussion on lead zirconate titanate (PZT) which is one of the most well-known ferroelectric materials that can be tuned to have antiferroelectric properties under certain conditions.
Finally, a short section is devoted to the antiferroelectric phase of silver.
Introduction
Ferroelectrics are polar insulating materials whose polarization, if polarized, is spontaneous (i.e., does not require any external electric field to maintain the polarization).
This polarization can be reversed with the application of an external field.
However, there exist some insulating materials which can exhibit polarization without external field but whose polarization can’t be reversed with an external field.
These are called antiferroelectrics.
In this report, the theory and applications of these materials will be discussed.
Antiferroelectricity
Antiferroelectricity is a type of magnetism where two adjacent dipoles are anti-aligned.
As mentioned before, antiferroelectric materials are insulators that have a polarization with spontaneous polarization, but it cannot be reversed with an external field.
Antiferroelectricity is characterized by the fact that it is impossible to apply an external field to reverse the polarization in the materials, and in its absence, it is a stable material.
The polarization is not parallel to the nearest neighbors but rather in opposition.
There are three phases of antiferroelectricity.
What is the Middle East?
Essay
The term "Middle East" is a geographical term that has been in use since the early 19th century but the definition of the region covered by this term has changed over time.
The Middle East is a term that has been used to refer to a region that covers South Western Asia although currently it includes some countries like Pakistan, North Africa and Caucasus (Brown, 2004).
It is not a country or even a continent; the Middle East is a geographical area, defined by the area between Europe and Far East and includes North African countries and Southern parts of Russia.

There is no single or official definition of the Middle East as far as the geography is concerned, though most authors agree that the region includes countries that are located within the area bounded roughly by the Ural Mountains in the north-west, Afghanistan and Pakistan in the east, Libya in the south-west, and Turkey in the north.
However, it is also common for some authors to include some of the North African countries in their Middle East definition.
In the US, the term “Middle East” was originally introduced by President Woodrow Wilson around 1918.
This was because the area between Europe and China was considered as part of the middle section of the earth.
However, the boundaries of the area have changed over the time.

For instance, during the Cold War, the United States Department of State and some other United States organizations would sometimes include Soviet countries, particularly the Caucasus, which includes Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan, and Central Asian countries within the Middle East.
Similarly, before World War II, France included North African states like Morocco, Tunisia, and Algeria within its Middle East definition.
Currently, most scholars include these states in what is referred to as "Greater Middle East."
### The Intersection of Identities and Experiences Case Study
The case tells about an elderly lesbian interracial couple, Ruth and Janice, who have been living together for 42 years in a small town in a Southern state.
However, due to a car accident that killed Janice, the local hospital decided to place her body in a hospital room and let her body decompose before it was picked up by her family.
Ruth had to deal with this problem.
In order to discuss the intersection of identities and experiences, we first need to define what these terms mean.
Then we can look at how identity affects experience and vice versa.
Let us begin.
#### Defining Key Terms
**Identity:** In psychology, an individual's identity is the collection of characteristics that make them unique.
Identity includes a person's name, gender, race, and religion, but also less obvious things such as a person’s friends, family, occupation, hobbies, beliefs, values, and so on.
**Experience:** Experience refers to the sum total of all events that have happened in a person's life.
In a psychological context, experience refers to a person's memories, thoughts, beliefs, feelings, and so on.
In a way, identity and experience are two sides of the same coin.
Experience makes up a part of your identity (because you are not who you were yesterday, and you will be a different person from who you are today in the future).
On the other hand, your identity is influenced by your experience, which is why your experience changes over time.
#### Case Background
Ruth and Janice were a lesbian couple, meaning that they identified as women but attracted towards each other and had sexual relations.
Also, Ruth and Janice were of different races, meaning that their ethnicity was different.
In a place in a small Southern American state, there may be cultural issues that prevent Ruth from being recognized as Janice’s wife.

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is the richest country in oil in the Middle East region.

The Kingdom has opened its markets to foreign investments two years ago and provided many investors with opportunities to invest in the largest stock exchange in the Middle East and North Africa, which is located there (the Saudi Stock Exchange, or Tadawul).
There are several reasons that could have led the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to open itself up to foreign investment:
* To increase revenue to support government spending
* To develop infrastructure such as highways, public transportation, schools, hospitals and other government projects.
* To improve the living standards of citizens and residents.

Foreign direct investment (FDI) in Saudi Arabia grew from $12 billion in 2017 to $24.2 billion in 2019 and was then estimated at $22.2 billion in 2020, with a decline mainly due to the impact of the ongoing coronavirus pandemic and low prices of crude oil, which affected all economies in the world.
In 2021, FDI increased to $35.8 billion; this amount of FDI is considered high by Saudi standards.
It also ranked in 2nd place in the Middle East for FDI as a share of GDP, after the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Saudi Arabia, the world’s second-largest oil exporter, also has the most ambitious economic program and strategy to diversify the sources of income and reduce its dependence on oil, which is called the Vision 2030 program.
This program will also help in providing better employment for young people in Saudi Arabia, who represent 65% of the total population.
Vision 2030 focuses on many areas such as:
1. Diversifying economy and increasing non-oil revenue
2. Increasing the number of women in the workforce
3. Improving the quality of life
Post September 11, 2001 Terrorist Attacks Essay
The September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on the twin towers in the United States of America really grieved the Muslim community in America with the effects being felt up to 20 years later.
The American Muslim population was one of the most affected groups and is still experiencing the impact.
It is important to examine the events that led to the attacks, how it affected the Muslims in the US and how they have coped with these effects.
Background
On September 11, 2001, the United States was the victim of the biggest terrorist attack in its history.
A total of 2996 people were killed in this incident.
The plane that hit the twin towers was piloted by five hijackers from Saudi Arabia.
Osama Bin Laden and Al-Qaeda were responsible for the execution of this attack on the World Trade Center.
Bin Ladin and his group claimed responsibility of this act and he also declared war on the Americans after 14 years.
He accused America of being the enemy and said that America and its ally were the enemies of Islam.
After the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on New York, America went into war with Afghanistan.
The reason behind this was that America wanted to find the place from where the attacks were being planned.
It was assumed that they were planned in Afghanistan.
But it was discovered that there are two terrorists who came to the US before and they planned this whole operation.
So, after the September 11 terrorist attacks, America also started targeting the Arabs as it was not possible to differentiate between the guilty and the innocent.
So, the Arabs in the US were treated the same way as the Arabs in other countries.
So, in the end, the whole Arab world became the target, and America started making war with them.
